intro: Step inside the Terrace Houses at Ephesus, lived in from the 1st to the 7th century AD. On the slope opposite Curetes Street stand six luxury residences, their floors in mosaic and their walls in fresco. They had underfloor heating, enclosed drains and glazed windows, and they are the one place that shows what a rich Roman's house was actually like in the first century AD. The model takes you inside one unit, around its colonnaded court.
spot-1: Now you are looking at the peristyle court, the colonnaded heart of the house. Everything turned towards it: the house took its light and its rainwater from here.
spot-2: Now look down at the impluvium, the pool in the middle of the court. It caught the rain running off the roof. Imagine the sound of it on a stormy day.
spot-3: Here you are looking at the fresco. The walls were painted on plaster, and the pictures in the House of the Muses still survive.
spot-4: Now lower your gaze to the mosaic floor. The floors of the rooms were laid with coloured stone tesserae, piece by tiny piece.
spot-5: And now the colonnade. The columns around the court did more than frame it: they carried the storey above as well.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. What is documented here is the material rather than the measurements. The source gives the number of residences, tells us that they rise two storeys, and that the floors are mosaic and the walls fresco — but not the size of any one room. So the court, the number of columns around it and the depth of the rooms are modelled from the known proportions of a Roman peristyle house. The fresco on the wall and the mosaics on the floor are photographs of these very houses, but the model does not show which picture belonged in which room. And one more thing: the real building now stands under a modern protective roof, which the model leaves off.
